_note: v2 hook overrides for l'hôtel, used only where the source hook breaks the content rules or differs from the painting. Source data is untouched.

fr_aventure_noun.hook: An old explorer in a pith helmet zooms through the lobby in a red pedal car, holding a map high above his head: what an ADVENTURE (ah-vahn-TEWR)!
fr_aventure_noun.why: The painting shows an old man explorer in a pedal car; the hook now describes him.

fr_visiteur_noun.hook: A VISITOR in a pith helmet with a feather in it rings the brass bell at the desk, waiting to be let in (vee-zee-TUHR).
fr_visiteur_noun.why: In the painting the visitor rings the bell (feather in his helmet) rather than tickling it.

fr_hotel_noun.hook: At the HOTEL desk a bellboy in a red cap leans in, gasping 'OH, TELL!' while the grey cat beside the guest book holds up a paper (oh-TEL).
fr_hotel_noun.why: Matches the painted bellboy and cat at the desk.

fr_hospitalite_noun.hook: A kind owl in a nurse's cap, as if from the HOSPITAL, pours TEA for a guest in a fluffy bathrobe at a little table: HOSPITALITY.
fr_hospitalite_noun.why: The respelling inside the source hook trips the content filter; same scene, respelling left to the card's pronunciation line.

fr_hotelier_noun.hook: 'HOTEL-YAY!' (oh-tuh-LYAY) cheers the lady in the sun hat as the HOTELIER in his navy suit, big ring of keys at his belt, hands her the brass room key.
fr_hotelier_noun.why: Masculine noun, male hotelier. Repainted so he hands a key to a grown-up guest instead of leaning over a child (content note b).

fr_palace_noun.hook: A LASS in a striped apron polishes a big model of a gleaming, gold-domed seaside LUXURY HOTEL (pah-LAHS): in French a palace is a grand hotel, not a royal palace.
fr_palace_noun.why: Adds the apron and model stand as painted; meaning unchanged.

fr_hammam_noun.hook: In the steamy archway of the HAMMAM an old lady in a white cap lounges in a hammock wrapped in a fluffy towel and sighs: 'AAH, MA'AM, how lovely!' (ah-MAHM)
fr_hammam_noun.why: The painting shows the old lady with her towel in the steamy bath-house arch, without an attendant.

fr_flanerie_noun.hook: A sleepy fellow in sky-blue FLANNEL pyjamas and felt slippers STROLLS idly round the terrace, hands behind his back (flah-nuh-REE).
fr_flanerie_noun.why: The painted stroller is a young sleepy fellow rather than a gentleman.

fr_periple_noun.hook: A duck paddles a long loop across the pool, leaving a RIPPLE trail behind it: a great JOURNEY (pay-REEPL).
fr_periple_noun.why: Matches the painted duck and ripples.

fr_recepteur_noun.hook: A guest in a bathrobe on a sun lounger presses the telephone RECEIVER to his ear in surprise, while a bluebird perches beside the telephone (ray-sehp-TUHR).
fr_recepteur_noun.why: The bluebird sits next to the telephone, not on it.

fr_reservation_noun.hook: A swan in a big sun hat checks her blank RESERVATION card at her table (ray-zehr-vah-SYOHN).
fr_reservation_noun.why: The painted swan wears a sun hat, not a flowered one.

fr_tripe_noun.hook: A stork waiter high-steps across the rug with a covered silver dish of TRIPE, as if setting off on a long TRIP (TREEP).
fr_tripe_noun.why: Steam is not clearly visible on the dish, so 'steaming' was dropped.

fr_deplacement_noun.hook: A badger businessMAN on a work TRIP lugs a suitcase so heavy that he can barely DISPLACE it across the floor (day-plahs-MAHN).
fr_deplacement_noun.why: The rug is not rucked in the painting; the hook keeps the heavy-suitcase movement.

fr_touristique_adj.hook: Two TOURIST mice with cameras round their necks squeak 'EEK!' at the model Eiffel Tower: how TOURISTY (too-rees-TEEK).
fr_touristique_adj.why: The painting shows two mice with one camera each instead of one mouse with three.

fr_disposition_noun.hook: A white poodle strikes a proud POSE on a little gold chair in a neat ARRANGEMENT of chairs: dis-POSE-ition.
fr_disposition_noun.why: Matches the painted poodle on one of the arranged chairs.

fr_tournee_noun.hook: A little animal band (fox trumpeter, cat accordionist, rabbit) rides along with a pony on TOUR; the pony rears up and NEIGHS (toor-NAY).
fr_tournee_noun.why: Matches the painted band and rearing pony.

fr_excursion_noun.hook: A donkey with a picnic basket on its saddle and a little red flag waits for the day's EXCURSION (ehk-skewr-SYOHN).
fr_excursion_noun.why: The painting shows one basket, so the hook no longer mentions two.

fr_invite_noun.hook: A young GUEST in a smart navy suit lifts his cup of TEA, a sealed invitation in his other hand: INVITE-TEA (an-vee-TAY).
fr_invite_noun.why: The painted guest is a boy holding a sealed (blank) invitation.
